subject: Materials Science
title: Quenching and Martensite
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Quenching and Martensite.

hook.text: A blacksmith plunges a glowing blade into water. Steam explodes. The steel becomes rock-hard.

buildup.text: At high temperature, iron atoms sit in a face-centered cubic arrangement called austenite.

discovery.text: Quenching traps carbon atoms that can't escape — they distort the lattice into martensite.

twist.text: Martensite is extremely hard but so brittle it can shatter like glass.

climax.text: That's why swords and springs are tempered after quenching — trading a little hardness for toughness.

punchline.text: Quenching freezes atoms in a panicked arrangement.

quiz.question: What is martensite?
options: A soft phase formed during slow cooling
A very hard phase formed by rapid quenching of steel
A type of rust that forms on steel
